key_insight: For structure-encoded tasks, finite example-only training can leave uncertainty that validated governing structure resolves by construction.
engineering_relevance: Embedding known operators, physical laws, or graph rules can constrain the hypothesis space, leaving learning to handle unspecified components.
method: Define the structure gap between structure-aware methods and example-only learners.
Prove excess-risk, cell-coverage, and unobserved-orbit limits.
Test mechanisms in inverse problems, sparse recovery, and graph reachability.
evidence_signal: The Gaussian inverse-problem analysis shows a known-operator Wiener solver attains Bayes risk while dense empirical linear learning retains expected excess risk; controlled experiments include graph size extrapolation.
watch_item: The argument depends on validated structure and does not establish a universal impossibility of closing the gap as data coverage grows.
paper_title: The Structure Gap: When More Data Cannot Replace Structured Reasoning
